speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: von Willebrand Disease

The clinical picture of mucous membrane bleeding (epistaxis, gum bleeding) with normal platelet count and normal PT/aPTT is classic for von Willebrand Disease. Since the child is 4 years old and has no history of prolonged surgical bleeding or umbilical cord hemorrhage, this may be a mild type that was previously undiagnosed. To confirm, I need to check the von Willebrand factor levels and activity.
